newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end mixed on cash disappointment.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end mixed on cash disappointment.

text.p: Reports that some central and southern Plains feedlots were selling cattle at $67 per cwt instead of the $68 that had been expected, weighed on CME live cattle futures which closed mostly lower, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.200 cent per lb higher to 0.375 lower with April off 0.225 at 67.950 cents. Feeder cattle ended up 0.025 to off 0.425 with only March up and May off most at 68.675 cents.

Expectations of firmer cash cattle prices had supported live cattle futures early, but futures slipped when cash cattle sold at $67. Rolling of long April positions into June underpinned the latter, traders said.

Packers raised bids for fed cattle to $67 per cwt early Thursday which sparked speculation that $68 will be paid soon because they were running short of slaughter supplies. But feedlots started to let their cattle go at the $67 level and futures in turn, slipped, they said.
However, trade remained light as market watchers awaited the quarterly USDA Hogs and Pigs report to be released after the close, sources said.
The Taiwan pork ban lent underlying support to deferred contracts. Export demand may partly switch to beef if the Taiwan ban boosts pork prices sharply in the months ahead, sources added.

General spreading of long June/short April added to selling by Prudential Securities, Rosenthal Collins and RBH in April. Cargill Investor Services and ADM Investor Services bought April early. RBH bought June, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, commercials bought August 60 puts and locals bought June 60 puts. Commission houses were selling April 68 puts and calls, pit sources added.
Feeder cattle futures were pressured by scattered selling following higher corn futures. This offset another gain in the latest CME feeder cattle index, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.12 at $69.47 per cwt.
Stone Traders sold May early while Cargill Investor Services lightly spread long May feeders/short October live cattle futures, pit sources said.
